description.text:
Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development.
It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways,
without incrementing the interface major version and without prior
notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients
and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols
and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or
semantics remaining stable across releases.

This protocol allows privileged clients to register and manage global
shortcuts for keyboard key sequences, touch swipe gestures, and touch
hold gestures. It also provides a one-shot shortcut capture facility
for clients that need to read the next shortcut input from the user.

Global shortcuts are managed in a per-user context. Shortcuts for
different users are isolated and will not interfere with each other.
This behavior is transparent to clients of this interface.

The terms "must", "must not", "should", and "may" in this document are
to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

A singleton global that manages global shortcut bindings for
key sequences, swipe gestures, and hold gestures.

Before registering or removing bindings the client must acquire
exclusive control by sending the acquire request. Only one client
may hold the manager at a time within a given user session.

Bindings are registered via bind_key, bind_swipe_gesture, and
bind_hold_gesture, and removed via unbind. All of these
requests take effect immediately. A bind request that cannot be
applied is reported with a bind_failure event; successful bind
and unbind requests generate no event, and the client can use
the wl_display.sync request to confirm that earlier requests
have been processed.

If the client's user session is not the currently active
session, bind and unbind requests are deferred: they are
applied when that session becomes active again.

Destroying the manager object implicitly releases the
exclusive control acquired via acquire; no separate release
request is needed.

The capture_next_shortcut request is independent of acquire and
may be sent at any time.

Destroy the shortcut manager object. If the client currently
holds exclusive control via acquire, that control is implicitly
released so another client may acquire it. Existing shortcut
bindings registered by this client remain active in the
compositor until the compositor or another client removes them.

Acquire exclusive control of the shortcut manager for this
client. The client must send this request before any bind_key,
bind_swipe_gesture, bind_hold_gesture, or unbind request.
Sending those requests without first acquiring is a
protocol error (not_acquired).

Only one client may hold the manager at a time within a given
user session. If another client already holds it, the
compositor sends a protocol error (occupied).

Exclusive control is released implicitly when the client
destroys the manager object.
description.summary: acquire exclusive control of the shortcut manager

description.text:
Register a key sequence binding. The binding takes effect
immediately.

The key argument uses the portable textual format of
QKeySequence (PortableText); see
https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qkeysequence.html#toString for the
format specification. Only combinations that form a valid
shortcut can be registered; see the capture_next_shortcut
request for the validity rules. An invalid combination is
reported with bind_failure and the invalid_argument error.

The name argument must be unique among all existing bindings.
If a binding with the same name already exists, this request
is reported with bind_failure and the name_conflict error.

If a binding with the same key sequence and action already
exists, this request updates its flags to the new value rather
than failing. This upsert-on-trigger semantics
applies only to bind_key; bind_swipe_gesture and
bind_hold_gesture treat duplicate trigger-action pairs as
errors.

Sending this request without first acquiring is a protocol
error (not_acquired).

args.name: name
args.summary: unique name for this keybinding

args.name: key
args.summary: key sequence in QKeySequence portable text format

args.name: flags
args.summary: trigger conditions for this keybinding

args.name: action
args.summary: compositor action to execute on activation

description.text:
Register a swipe gesture binding. The binding takes effect
immediately.

The name argument must be unique among all existing bindings.
If a binding with the same name already exists, this request
is reported with bind_failure and the name_conflict error.

If a binding with the same finger count, direction, and action
already exists, this request is reported with bind_failure
and the duplicate_binding error.

If direction is not one of the defined direction enum values,
this request is reported with bind_failure and the
invalid_argument error.

Sending this request without first acquiring is a protocol
error (not_acquired).

args.name: name
args.summary: unique name for this swipe gesture binding

args.name: finger
args.summary: number of fingers required for the swipe

args.name: direction
args.summary: required swipe direction

args.name: action
args.summary: compositor action to execute on activation

description.text:
Remove the binding identified by name. The removal takes
effect immediately. If no binding with the given name exists,
this request is silently ignored.

Sending this request without first acquiring is a protocol
error (not_acquired).

args.name: name
args.summary: name of the binding to remove

description.text:
Create a treeland_shortcut_capture_v3 object and start a
one-shot capture of the next shortcut input. This request
does not require acquire and does not modify existing
bindings.

The surface argument must be a wl_surface owned by the
requesting client. If it is not, the compositor sends a
protocol error (invalid_surface).

The compositor handles at most one capture at a time,
regardless of which client requested it. A capture is also
considered in progress until the compositor has consumed the
key_release of the last captured key, so that the release
cannot trigger a shortcut bound in the meantime. If a capture
is already in progress, the compositor emits failed with
reason busy on the newly created object immediately after
creation.

If the seat argument is not null, the compositor verifies
that the keyboard focus of that seat is on the surface. If
the seat argument is null, the compositor selects a seat
whose keyboard focus is on the surface. If no seat has
keyboard focus on the surface, the compositor emits failed
with reason not_active on the newly created object
immediately after creation. Clients must be prepared to
handle a capture object that fails immediately.

Input from seats other than the validated seat is not
intercepted and is processed normally. On the validated seat
the capture intercepts input with priority over registered
shortcut bindings.

While the capture is pending, input from the validated seat
is handled as follows. If the surface loses keyboard focus,
the compositor emits failed with reason aborted and lets the
current event continue to its new focus target. Auto-repeat
events are consumed silently. A pointer button or wheel
event terminates the capture with reason interrupted and is
consumed. A key_press of a pure modifier key (Ctrl, Alt,
Shift, and similar) is consumed silently; its key_release
terminates the capture with reason interrupted, unless the
key is the Meta (Super) key: releasing Meta with no other
modifier held emits captured with the shortcut "Meta". A
key_press of any other key terminates the capture immediately
on the press. If the pressed combination is a valid shortcut
the compositor emits captured and consumes the key_release
that follows; otherwise it emits failed with reason
interrupted. In the captured and interrupted cases the
triggering input event is consumed and not forwarded to any
client.

A valid shortcut is one of: a non-modifier key combined with
Ctrl, Alt, or Meta; a standalone function key (F1 to F35); a
standalone key such as Delete, Backspace, Pause, Print,
Insert, Help, Menu, or Cancel; Shift combined with Space,
Escape, Tab, or a navigation key (Home, End, PageUp, PageDown,
and arrows); a standalone media, browser, brightness, or
launch key; or the Meta (Super) key pressed alone. An
unmodified alphanumeric key and an unmodified Escape are not
valid shortcuts.

args.name: surface
args.summary: surface used to validate keyboard focus

args.name: seat
args.summary: seat to capture from, or null to capture from any available seat

args.name: capture
args.summary: one-shot capture object

description.text:
Emitted when a binding registered with action notify is
activated. The name argument identifies the binding by its
unique name. The flags argument indicates which key event
triggered the activation, using the keybind_flag enum values.

args.name: name
args.summary: name of the activated binding

args.name: flags
args.summary: key event type that triggered activation

description.text:
Emitted when a bind_key, bind_swipe_gesture, or
bind_hold_gesture request could not be applied; the rejected
binding has no effect. The name argument identifies the
rejected binding; the error argument provides the reason.

If the requesting client's session is not active, the bind
request is applied (and possibly rejected) only when that
session becomes active again, so this event may be emitted
long after the request was sent. Each rejected request is
reported separately; other bindings of the same client are
not affected.

args.name: name
args.summary: name of the rejected binding

args.name: error
args.summary: reason for the failure

description.text:
Flags that control when a key binding fires relative to the
key event lifecycle.

key_press: fires when the key is pressed.
key_release: fires when the key is released.
repeat: fires repeatedly while the key is held down
(auto-repeat). Only meaningful when combined with
key_press; combining with key_release causes both
the press and the release auto-repeat events to fire.

Common combinations:
- key_press only: fires once on press; ignores repeat and release.
- key_press | repeat: fires on press and on every auto-repeat tick.
- key_press | key_release: fires on press and release;
auto-repeat events are ignored.
- key_press | key_release | repeat: fires on press, every
auto-repeat tick, and on release.

entries.summary: trigger on key press

entries.name: key_release
entries.summary: trigger on key release

entries.name: repeat
entries.summary: trigger on auto-repeat while the key is held

description.text:
Represents a single pending request to capture the next shortcut
input from the user, created by
treeland_shortcut_manager_v3.capture_next_shortcut.

The compositor captures input once and emits at most one terminal
event: either captured or failed. After a terminal event is sent
this object becomes inert; the client should destroy it promptly.

If the client destroys this object while capture is still pending,
the capture is cancelled and no terminal event is sent.

Destroy this capture object. If capture is still pending,
destroying the object cancels it; no terminal event will be
sent after this request is processed.

Emitted when the compositor captured one shortcut input for
this request. The key argument carries the shortcut sequence
in the same QKeySequence portable text format used by
treeland_shortcut_manager_v3.bind_key. A capture of the Meta
(Super) key pressed alone is reported as the shortcut "Meta".

This is a terminal event; the object is now inert.

args.name: key
args.summary: captured shortcut sequence in QKeySequence portable text format

description.text:
Emitted when the compositor could not deliver a captured
shortcut. The reason argument describes why. See the
failed_reason enum for details.

This is a terminal event; the object is now inert.
description.summary: the capture could not be completed

args.name: reason
args.summary: reason the capture failed

description.text:

description.summary: reasons a one-shot capture could not complete
